title: What if the Saudis Break the Petrodollar System- - Luke Gromen's Prescient Predictions from 2022

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/What if the Saudis Break the Petrodollar System- - Luke Gromen's Prescient Predictions from 2022.docx
meta.transcript source: YouTube auto-captions (no punctuation on this video's captions)

speakers: Host (The Intrinsic Value Podcast / Investor's Podcast Network, unnamed in captions)
summary: Recorded Jan 2022: Gromen argues this is not a normal tightening cycle: sovereign debt bubble, peak cheap energy/metals, China water/power limits and US-China cold war imply sticky inflation. The Fed is trapped by the dollar and bond market; the debt can only be handled via negative real rates, capital flows decide the dollar, Saudi yuan oil is inevitable, and he explains reverse repo/Basel III plumbing.

completeness_estimate: 0.86 - the first reader captured nearly all of the macro, China water and plumbing arguments with accurate numbers; missed a few reasoning steps, caveats and time-bound data points and had no factual errors that I could find.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: the tightening cycle is occurring in the context of a bunch of things that no one alive has ever invested through
claims.claim: The 2022 Fed tightening is not an ordinary rate cycle: it coincides with a pandemic recovery, a bursting global sovereign debt bubble, peak cheap energy and metals, and a US-China cold war, so old playbooks fail.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: we think you're going to need negative real rates on a sustained basis increasingly negative to make Global sovereign debt and fiscal positions and entitlement obligations in the West in particular sustainable
claims.claim: Western debt and entitlements are only sustainable with sustained, increasingly negative real rates.
claims.direction: long inflation-protected assets, gold; short nominal bonds

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: you're going to have a real sort of sustained inflationary impulse from uh from commodity and metals markets
claims.claim: Peak cheap energy and metals (falling ore grades) means higher prices are needed for supply, creating a persistent commodity inflation impulse.
claims.indicator: energy and metals prices, ore grades

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: to be blunt if China has a water problem China has a power problem and if China has a power problem the world has a power problem and the world has an inflation problem
claims.claim: Chinese water constraints become a power shortage, which hits the world's factory and exports inflation.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: none of them in singularly or in aggregate ever uh had an economic clout such that their GDP was 60 or more of the United States as GDP and china hit that level in 2014.
claims.claim: China is a different adversary from the USSR: GDP above 60% of US since 2014 and the US offshored manufacturing to it, so trade and supply-chain frictions will be stickier than expected.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: we have a a technology that is moving faster and faster and forcing deflation on the system which is a problem because the system is dead back and needs uh exponential inflation
claims.claim: Technology deflation conflicts with a debt-backed system that needs inflation (Jeff Booth), a two-horses-one-ass tension that will force policy choices.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: we know the World War II Playbook right we saw last time that the GDP got this high they let inflation on hot they cap yields uh from 46 to 51
claims.claim: The only precedent for debt this high is 1946-51, when authorities capped yields and let inflation run (real rates as low as -14%), cutting debt/GDP from 110% to 55%; Gromen says the Fed should do the same rather than tighten.
claims.direction: long gold/real assets, short bondholders in real terms

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: foreigners are not buying enough treasuries um relative to what we're emitting
claims.claim: The US has a structural balance of payments problem: large current account deficits and insufficient foreign Treasury buying.
claims.indicator: current account deficit, foreign Treasury demand

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: going from 135 to 122 took seven percent CPI it took it broke Supply chains
claims.claim: Debt/GDP fell from 135% to 122% only at the cost of 7% CPI and broken supply chains, so deleveraging via inflation is hard in a stretched system.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: I've been watching the dollar trade down with real rates rising in the last week week and a half I've been watching gold rise with real rates Rising sharply in the U.S
claims.claim: Dollar and gold rising/falling the wrong way versus rising real rates is a signal of capital flows dominating rate differentials.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: instead of sterilizing U.S deficits via treasury buying they've been sterilizing deficits by buying U.S stocks
claims.claim: Per Druckenmiller, foreigners have financed US deficits by buying US tech stocks rather than Treasuries.
claims.indicator: foreign flows into US equities vs Treasuries

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: if they start moving money out of tech that means Capital flows that are helping Finance these deficits sterilize these deficits start flowing Elsewhere on the margin and the release valve turns into the dollar
claims.claim: If post-pandemic rotation moves money out of tech into cyclicals/value, the capital flows financing the deficit leave and the dollar becomes the release valve.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: corn Holdings of equities has gone from like 2 trillion in 2009 to 12 trillion in 2020
claims.claim: Foreign holdings of US equities rose from about $2 trillion in 2009 to $12 trillion in 2020 (FRED).

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: if the dollar gets weaker that's only going to put more upward pressure on inflation and force the FED to tighten more
claims.claim: A weaker dollar adds inflation pressure and forces the Fed to tighten more, a feedback loop.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: the price of oil encyclicals and gold and all this other stuff is going to have to rise a whole lot um to sort of balance those current account deficits
claims.claim: If global capital shifts from US tech to oil, industrials and gold, their prices must rise a lot to balance current account deficits.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: rates are gonna go up Dollar's gonna go up markets are going to go down
claims.claim: An aggressive Fed move (shrinking the $9T balance sheet fast) would lift rates and the dollar and hurt markets.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: I think with the dollar at 96 at 97 the dollar certainly and a hundred were
claims.claim: How high yields can go depends on the dollar: with DXY 96-100 and above the bond market gets close to breaking (stocks, oil and bonds sell together).

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: the yield curve where it's you know flat and you know flattening out um is probably telling you that that we're getting close
claims.claim: A flattening yield curve signals that the bond market is near its tolerance for tightening.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: if you take it down to 70 over the next 12 months then I think you probably can you probably can hit some of these numbers
claims.claim: The Fed can only deliver the expected four hikes and balance sheet runoff if the dollar falls sharply (DXY toward 70-80).

claims.speaker: Host
claims.quote: I just don't know that these International markets uh could possibly allow for the dollar of the Fall that that far
claims.claim: The dollar is zero sum: other central banks may ease to stop their currencies strengthening so the dollar falls only so far.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: who needs Tech at 40 times sales
claims.claim: With the pandemic becoming endemic, investors can buy cheap cyclicals/value instead of tech at 40 times sales, so capital leaves the NASDAQ.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: there's an inverse relationship between the level of a dollar and and how many treasuries they buy and once it gets too high they sell a whole lot and once it gets low enough they start buying again
claims.claim: Foreign Treasury buying is inversely related to the dollar level: they sell when the dollar is high and buy when it is low, which can cap a dollar decline.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: you sell growth you buy value you buy Commodities you buy Emerging Markets you sell the United States and the dollar Falls
claims.claim: If the cyclical capital flow trade plays out: sell growth, buy value, commodities and EM, sell US and the dollar.

claims.speaker: Host
claims.quote: it looks like you could maybe have an inversion on the bond you'll curve out here in July of 22
claims.claim: Host extrapolates yield trend lines across maturities to a curve inversion around July 2022 with 30-year yield at most about 2.7%.
claims.indicator: trend lines on yields by maturity

claims.speaker: Host
claims.quote: we are deeply under that 40-year trend of How High those yields would sell off to
claims.claim: Yields are far below the 40-year downtrend line yet markets are already struggling, which shows how little rate increase the system can bear.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: you actually have you know working-class wages Rising above inflation for the first time in like 20 years
claims.claim: Working-class wages rose faster than inflation for the first time in about 20 years, though politicians want inflation lower before midterms.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: US is facing a very similar problem that Germany was facing in 1931
claims.claim: Like Germany in 1931 the US has external and entitlement obligations that it cannot print its way out of, plus de-industrialization and great power competition.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: they should be letting inflation run hot they should be screwing bondholders they should on a real basis um and capping yields
claims.claim: Bondholders must pay either in real terms (inflation plus yield caps) or nominal terms (austerity); Germany chose austerity with disastrous political results.
claims.direction: short long bonds in real terms

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: they have been drawing on way in excess of replenishment rate
claims.claim: China's northern aquifers are being drained far faster than they replenish (tens of thousands of years), so the constraint is structural not weather-driven.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: here in 4q21 we have apple being asked to shut down factories for the first time in decades in China for lack of power
claims.claim: Evidence of power rationing: 3Q21 plant shutdowns, Apple factory shutdowns in 4Q21 and Bitcoin mining migration, which Gopal Reddy ties to water-driven power scarcity.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: this water is endemic to electric power and in general electric power is endemic to China's economic growth
claims.claim: Water scarcity cuts hydro base-load and raises water-intensive coal and nuclear needs, so it links directly to China's output.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: the short answer is is within a couple years
claims.claim: The water-power problem could cause major issues within a couple of years, possibly late 2022, but good rain could delay it.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: if China's got water problems there's like zero chance we've seen Peak
claims.claim: Consensus that supply-chain disruption has peaked is wrong because the China water problem makes shortages endemic.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: companies are going to go from running jit to doing what they did in the 70s I'm told which is you order as much as you can
claims.claim: Endemic shortages move companies from just-in-time to hoarding inventory (as in the 1970s), which feeds an inflationary mindset the Fed cannot fix without crashing the economy.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: because the FED can't tighten enough to fight this without blowing up the bond market with the dollar where it is
claims.claim: The Fed is stuck: tightening enough to fight supply-driven inflation would break the bond market at the current dollar level.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: once reserves get too high according to Basel III banking regulations the banks can actually have too higher reserves
claims.claim: QE hits a limit: when reserves are too high Basel III forces banks to cut balance sheet, so QE has declining marginal utility for lending.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: once they have too many reserves they have to stop growing their balance sheet elsewhere
claims.claim: Beyond some point QE reduces banks' ability to lend because reserves count against balance sheet limits.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: the repo rate Spike people say well that was that was just a plumbing issue no that was that was them bumping up against this constraint
claims.claim: Basel III is meant to prevent central banks and the domestic banking system from financing deficits endlessly, and the 2019 repo spike was banks hitting that constraint.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: the reverse repo balance started really to blow out last April when the SLR the supplementary leverage ratio um exemption for treasuries that was put in place April of 2020
claims.claim: The reverse repo program grew from zero to $2 trillion in eight months after the SLR exemption expired, as a way to move reserves off bank balance sheets (like Enron's barge window dressing).

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: then what Zero Hedge said is I don't think correct in terms of no net flow implication
claims.claim: Zero Hedge's claim that the Fed can drain $1.5T via reverse repo with no impact is wrong unless the SLR exemption is renewed, because banks remain constrained on reserves and Treasuries.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: it's a classic Emerging Markets move you've seen it in Argentina
claims.claim: Changing bank and liquidity regulations to keep financing deficits is a classic balance-of-payments-problem response.

claims.speaker: Host
claims.quote: we're going to have these big deflationary fits they're going to step in with just arm loads of quantitative easing
claims.claim: Host expects recurring deflationary fits (like March 2020) met by large QE, UBI and eventually yield curve control.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: yield curve control is the Hotel California right once they check in they can never leave
claims.claim: The Fed will avoid yield curve control because it cannot be exited, preferring yield curve management.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: yield curve bumper bowling is what they're doing
claims.claim: The Fed already intervenes within a band: the 2019 repo spike was fixed in 24-48 hours by expanding the balance sheet, so the balance sheet is the release valve.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: because now you're going to be talking about uh CPI that's probably going to run seven to ten for the next two three four years
claims.claim: If supply constraints are structural, CPI could run 7-10% for 2-4 years, a very different case from cyclical recovery inflation.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: there's going to be a ton of inflation with all those things
claims.claim: ESG and climate-change initiatives add inflation.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: the Saudis are ultimately going to have to do uh what they must to keep their biggest client happy and their biggest client by far is China
claims.claim: Saudi Arabia will eventually concede oil sales to China in yuan because China is its largest customer.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: the world would no longer need to hold dollars for oil
claims.claim: Yuan-priced oil sales would remove dollar demand from oil buying, while the US keeps issuing deficits, so structurally the dollar weakens (Saudi riyal might fall, lowering oil costs in the short run).

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: when the FED buys 60 to 100 issuance the dollar goes down
claims.claim: Empirically, when the Fed absorbs 60-100% of Treasury issuance the dollar falls (March 2020 to April 2021).
claims.indicator: Fed QE share of issuance, DXY
claims.direction: short dollar when Fed buys issuance

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: what we're watching with fed tightening is them slowing the rate at which the dollar Falls
claims.claim: Gromen reframes Fed hikes as slowing the dollar's fall, and the lower the dollar goes the more room the Fed has to hike.

claims.speaker: Host
claims.quote: you're actually getting uh it's looking like a little bit of a roll over here on the macd
claims.claim: Host shows the monthly DXY MACD rolling over, consistent with momentum fading.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: if a dollar goes up this whole thing is going to implode
claims.claim: All major players need the dollar lower because a rising dollar would collapse the debt system.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: if you get gold just marching up you know that that can sort of create a framework to sort of try to get the dollar moving in a direction
claims.claim: The BIS and Treasury's Exchange Stabilization Fund could bid gold to push the dollar down; gold's rise in Jan 2022 fits.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: every six weeks Central Bankers accounting for 55 to 65 percent of the world's gross domestic product get together in a room in Basel Switzerland
claims.claim: Central bankers coordinate at the BIS (per a 2012 WSJ article) on keeping the dollar from rising, so policy is coordinated.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: a greater recognition amongst people sitting in senior seats that realize that the FED is trapped
claims.claim: Bill Miller's 50% Bitcoin / 50% Amazon portfolio and Dalio's 2% Bitcoin signal that senior investors expect the Fed to be trapped.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: fully reserving the euro dollar system means fed balance sheet 70 to 100 trillion
claims.claim: Resolving the deflation-vs-debt conflict requires the Fed to fully reserve the offshore dollar system, a $70-100 trillion balance sheet.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: people were selling gold and buying German race marks
claims.claim: In Weimar hyperinflation, investors sold gold to buy marks on rate-hike promises, which is the wrong bet; Gromen urges careful leverage (the path was the path).

claims.speaker: Host
claims.quote: a lot of the covid policies and things like that were actually causing a breakdown in Supply chains and then that caused prices to go up
claims.claim: Host argues pandemic policies broke supply chains first and that pushed prices up; Gromen says the order does not matter: running demand as hot as the stimulus did overloaded stretched supply chains, so demand-led deleveraging by inflation is capped by supply capacity.
claims.conditions: Applies when supply chains are stretched and just-in-time.
claims.testable: partly - decomposing supply and demand inflation is model-dependent

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: if they tighten before they deliver enough um they'll blow up they'll blow up markets they'll blow up the system
claims.claim: Because the dollar is a debt-backed system with a huge eurodollar layer rather than a gold-backed one, the Fed can only normalize after debt/GDP has fallen; tightening first breaks markets, which is why letting inflation run hot is needed more now than after WWII.
claims.conditions: Holds while debt/GDP is stretched and the system is leveraged.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: so much of it is entitlements defense interest not these things you can't cut
claims.claim: US deficits are structural (entitlements, defense, interest) and cannot be cut, so the financing need persists and has to be matched in the capital account by foreign purchases of tech stocks or Treasuries.
claims.indicator: US federal deficit composition and capital account
claims.conditions: Weakens only if foreigners keep buying either tech stocks or Treasuries.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: it's very possible we're just seeing sort of uh a small move you know counters cyclical move
claims.claim: Gromen admits the dollar's drop may be only a small counter-cyclical move and that it is too early to tell; the outcome depends on how aggressive the Fed is (a fast balance-sheet cut would push rates and the dollar up and markets down).
claims.indicator: dollar index vs Fed balance-sheet path
claims.direction: dollar down if tech outflows continue; up if Fed aggressive
claims.conditions: Two competing dynamics: unusual cycle versus normal tightening.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: we haven't been below 80 since 2014
claims.claim: On 12 January 2022 DXY was about 94 (high 97, about 89 a year earlier, range-bound until May-June 2021, then up after the Fed turned hawkish), and it had not been below 80 since 2014, so Gromen's 70-80 scenario means an extreme move.
claims.direction: dollar needs to fall far for the Fed to deliver four hikes

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: if they want to taper they're selling treasuries Ben needs a buyer
claims.claim: Countries resisting currency strength buy Treasuries, which is exactly what the Fed needs as it tapers and stops buying; foreign Treasury buying therefore rises as the dollar falls, which limits the dollar decline and supports Fed tightening.
claims.indicator: foreign official Treasury purchases vs dollar
claims.direction: foreign buying of Treasuries up as dollar falls
claims.conditions: Works if foreigners lean against their own currency strength.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: when it comes to economy and environment the economy wins full stop
claims.claim: Because China always prioritizes growth over the environment, power-plant shutdowns in 3Q21 presented as environmental are read as evidence of a real power shortage; Bitcoin miners are the first load to be shed when electricity is scarce.
claims.conditions: Inference from behaviour, not from direct data.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: there were articles you can find them online they were asking their citizens to start rationing water
claims.claim: In December 2021 Shenzhen and Guangzhou, the main tech manufacturing region, asked citizens to ration water, which Gromen cites as a further 'shark sighting' of acute water stress.
claims.direction: supply-chain risk from Chinese manufacturing hubs
claims.conditions: Rain could delay the problem for years.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: I think ultimately they'll be forced to uh I think it will be the last thing they want to do
claims.claim: Gromen thinks the Fed will eventually be forced into yield curve control because yield curve management gets tighter, but it will delay it as long as possible; the timing depends on inflation and growth.
claims.indicator: yield curve control by the Fed
claims.conditions: Triggered by an inflationary downdraft or bond selloff that the system cannot bear.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: I heard very credible Rumblings 18 months ago that the Chinese and Saudis signed a deal
claims.claim: Gromen cites credible rumours of a mid-2020 China-Saudi deal for some oil to be paid in yuan or dollars at China's choice, unconfirmed, with GCC ministers visiting China, so the move away from dollar oil pricing is probably under way and the open question is disclosure.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: it might actually be good for the dollar in the short run it might be bad for oil in the short run
claims.claim: A yuan oil deal is structurally negative for the dollar (less foreign demand, the Fed must absorb issuance) but could be dollar-positive and oil-negative in the short run, so market impact is uncertain.
claims.indicator: dollar and oil after a petrodollar break
claims.conditions: Short run versus structural effects differ.

claims.speaker: Luke Gromen
claims.quote: they don't have the Mandate where they need to manage the chips um in a more short-term nature
claims.claim: Aggressive end-game bets such as 50% Bitcoin are viable only for owners without short-term mandates or quarterly reporting; others have to manage position size and drawdown tolerance because losses of 30% would force exits.
claims.conditions: Depends on mandate, liquidity needs and leverage; Gromen warns 'be careful with leverage'.
